readme:
# DAgger 专家混合与访问状态聚合

## 1. 问题

实现逐状态专家混合，以及保留所有历史轮次的数据聚合。

提取 DAgger Algorithm 3.1 的数据闭环；标量线性环境中重新拟合策略，不实现完整交互式专家或分类器。

## 2. 核心公式

$$
\pi_i=\beta_i\pi^*+(1-\beta_i)\hat\pi_i,\qquad D\leftarrow D\cup\{(s,\pi^*(s))\}.
$$

## 3. 公式到代码

- `mixture_actions(expert: Tensor, learner: Tensor, draws: Tensor, beta: float) -> Tensor`
- `aggregate_dataset(old_states: Tensor, old_labels: Tensor, states: Tensor, labels: Tensor) -> tuple`

对同一状态只选择一个策略的动作，不能将两者数值平均。聚合沿样本轴追加，旧标签必须保留。专家为学习者访问的状态重新标注，标签不是实际执行的混合动作。

## 4. 本题约定

动作 expert/learner 为 (B,A)，draws 为 (B,) 且位于 [0,1)；draw<beta 时选专家。旧/新状态分别 (N,S)/(M,S)，标签 (N,A)/(M,A)；N可为0，M必须大于0。聚合结果脱离计算图；混合动作保留被选分支的梯度。

校验辅助函数已提供。浮点输入为有限 CPU float32/float64，不修改输入；非法形状、类型、范围或掩码必须抛出 `ValueError`。

## 5. 交互图与确定性实验

从只包含零状态的初始数据出发，滚动收集8个初始状态各8步轨迹，四轮聚合并最小二乘拟合反馈增益；比较12步自由执行的状态能量。

可视化由 `viz/gen.py` 生成；T3 将你的函数传入同一实验并记录真实指标。这是小规模确定性教学实验，不是机器人基准成绩。

## 6. 在网页中运行

在右侧 Python 编辑器中补全实现，点击 **运行测试**。查看失败测试的原因、期望值与实际值，修改代码后再次运行。所有必要测试通过后，题目会标记为已完成并解锁坑点讲解。

## 7. 来源与延伸

- [A Reduction of Imitation Learning and Structured Prediction to No-Regret Online Learning](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v15/ross11a.html) — Algorithm 3.1: mixed roll-in policy and aggregation of expert-labeled visited states

核验日期：2026-10-28。扩展到完整论文系统还需要本题范围中明确省略的模型、数据和环境。
notes:
# DAgger: 题解与易错点

对同一状态只选择一个策略的动作，不能将两者数值平均。聚合沿样本轴追加，旧标签必须保留。专家为学习者访问的状态重新标注，标签不是实际执行的混合动作。

beta=0完全使用学习者，beta=1完全使用专家。用显式均匀抽样值让分支可重复。数据集不携带旧策略计算图，避免跨轮累积无用梯度。

## 测试捕获的错误

- A policy mixture incorrectly averages action vectors.
- Aggregation discards every previous round.

## 实验范围

提取 DAgger Algorithm 3.1 的数据闭环；标量线性环境中重新拟合策略，不实现完整交互式专家或分类器。

## 可重复实验记录

8个初态、每轮8步、4轮，初始2个零样本；最小二乘反馈拟合，无随机采样。初始增益0，要求最终12步状态能量<初始的5%，样本数258，反馈增益=-0.6。

判题固定seed=42。计算采用CPU float64、显式输入，涉及优化时使用普通梯度更新；不下载数据集或模型权重。原生PyTorch与真实Pyodide/NumPy-WASM执行同一套T0–T3测试。阈值针对本教学实验。

en.title: DAgger Expert Mixtures and Visited-State Aggregation
en.readme:
# DAgger Expert Mixtures and Visited-State Aggregation

## 1. Exercise goal

Implement per-state expert mixing and retain every previous round of labeled states.

Isolate Algorithm 3.1 in a scalar linear environment with policy refitting; no interactive human expert or full classifier.

## 2. Core equations

$$
\pi_i=\beta_i\pi^*+(1-\beta_i)\hat\pi_i,\qquad D\leftarrow D\cup\{(s,\pi^*(s))\}.
$$

## 3. From equations to code

- `mixture_actions(expert: Tensor, learner: Tensor, draws: Tensor, beta: float) -> Tensor`
- `aggregate_dataset(old_states: Tensor, old_labels: Tensor, states: Tensor, labels: Tensor) -> tuple`

Select one policy action per state rather than averaging action vectors. Concatenate on the sample axis and retain old labels. Expert labels belong to states visited by the learner; they are not the executed mixture actions.

## 4. Contract and boundaries

Expert/learner actions are (B,A); draws is (B,) in [0,1), and draws<beta selects the expert. Old/new states are (N,S)/(M,S), labels (N,A)/(M,A), N>=0 and M>0. Aggregated data detach all inputs; selected mixture branches preserve gradients.

Validation helpers are provided. All floating inputs are finite CPU float32/float64; do not mutate inputs. Invalid shape, dtype, range or mask arguments raise `ValueError`.

## 5. Deterministic experiment and visualization

Starting from zero-state data, collect eight-step trajectories from eight starts for four aggregation rounds and fit a feedback gain by least squares; compare twelve-step state energy.

The visualization is generated by `viz/gen.py`; T3 runs the same experiment with your functions and records its actual metrics. These are small deterministic teaching results, not a robot benchmark.

## 6. Run your implementation

Complete the functions in the Python editor on the right, then click **Run tests**. Inspect each failed check, update your implementation, and run again. Passing every required check marks the problem as solved and unlocks the notes.

## 7. Sources and extensions

- [A Reduction of Imitation Learning and Structured Prediction to No-Regret Online Learning](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v15/ross11a.html) — Algorithm 3.1: mixed roll-in policy and aggregation of expert-labeled visited states

Verified 2026-10-28. Extending this operator to the full paper requires the omitted model, data and environment described in the scope above.
en.notes:
# DAgger: Solution notes

Select one policy action per state rather than averaging action vectors. Concatenate on the sample axis and retain old labels. Expert labels belong to states visited by the learner; they are not the executed mixture actions.

Beta zero uses only the learner and beta one only the expert. Explicit uniform draws make selection reproducible. The dataset does not retain previous policy graphs.

## Mistakes caught by the tests

- A policy mixture incorrectly averages action vectors.
- Aggregation discards every previous round.

## Experimental scope

Isolate Algorithm 3.1 in a scalar linear environment with policy refitting; no interactive human expert or full classifier.

## Reproducible protocol

Eight starts, eight steps per round, four rounds, two initial zero examples; least-squares feedback fit with explicit draws. Gain starts at zero. Require final twelve-step state energy below 5% of baseline, 258 examples, and gain -0.6.

The judge fixes seed 42. All calculations use CPU float64, explicit inputs and plain gradient updates where applicable; no datasets or model weights are downloaded. Native PyTorch and actual Pyodide/NumPy-WASM run the same T0–T3 suite. Thresholds refer to this teaching adaptation.
